revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Light Show Cost
revealWordProblem.text: Akela runs the light show for the concert. The cost of the light rig is given by the expression 75 + 9p, where p is the number of stage lights used. If Akela uses 8 stage lights, what is the cost of the light rig? Show how you substitute and evaluate.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Substitute p = 8 into 75 + 9p: 75 + 9(8). Multiply first: 9 × 8 = 72. Then add: 75 + 72 = 147. The light rig costs $147.

turnAndTalk.question: The concert cost is 150 + 12s, where s is the number of speakers. How do you find the cost for 5 speakers, and why does this one expression work for any number of speakers?

turnAndTalk.question: When you evaluate an expression like 4x² + 3, what order do you follow, and why must you square before you multiply?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Follow order of operations: substitute, then exponents, then multiply, then add.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer substitutes the value first, then applies the exponent before multiplying (e.g., 4 × 2² = 4 × 4 = 16, not (4 × 2)² ), citing order of operations.
turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate evaluates 4x² + 3 at x = 2 as (4 × 2)² + 3 = 67. Critique the error and give the correct value.

vocabulary.term: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
vocabulary.termEs: Escribir y evaluar expresiones numéricas con exponentes
vocabulary.definition: Turning a situation into a number sentence without an equal sign, then finding its value in the correct order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Convertir una situación en una expresión numérica sin signo de igual y luego hallar su valor en el orden correcto.

vocabulary.definition: A math phrase built from numbers and operations, with no equal sign and no variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una frase matemática hecha de números y operaciones, sin signo de igual y sin variable.
vocabulary.visual: 4 × 20 is an expression; 4 × 20 = 80 is an equation

vocabulary.definition: To find the single value an expression is worth by carrying out its operations in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar el único valor que representa una expresión, realizando sus operaciones en orden.

vocabulary.definition: The agreed order for evaluating: grouping symbols, then exponents, then multiply and divide left to right, then add and subtract left to right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El orden acordado para evaluar: signos de agrupación, luego exponentes, luego multiplicar y dividir de izquierda a derecha, y por último sumar y restar de izquierda a derecha.

vocabulary.definition: A short way to write repeated multiplication of the same factor, such as 2³ for 2 × 2 × 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma corta de escribir la multiplicación repetida del mismo factor, como 2³ para 2 × 2 × 2.

vocabulary.definition: In a power, the number being multiplied by itself. In 2³ the base is 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: En una potencia, el número que se multiplica por sí mismo. En 2³ la base es 2.

vocabulary.definition: In a power, the small raised number that says how many times the base is used as a factor.
vocabulary.definitionEs: En una potencia, el número pequeño elevado que indica cuántas veces se usa la base como factor.

launch.narrative: The studio's booking sheet lists a price for each kind of seat. Writing one numerical expression for the whole order — and evaluating it in the right order — is faster and easier to check than adding costs one at a time. Some counts are written as powers, so the exponent has to be handled before any multiplying.

conceptIntro.heading: Write the expression, then evaluate it in order
conceptIntro.intro: A numerical expression is a math phrase made of numbers and operations, with no equal sign. Writing one for a whole situation keeps every part visible; evaluating it means finding its single value, following the order of operations.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Evaluate in this order: grouping symbols, then powers, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right.

iDo.title: Watch me price the theater order
lines: Sofia buys 2 member tickets at $15, 4 non-member tickets at $20, and 8 student tickets at $2 each. I write one expression for each ticket type: 2 × 15, 4 × 20, and 8 × 2.
The whole order is the three costs added together: 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2.
Now I evaluate. There are no grouping symbols and no powers yet, so multiplication comes first, left to right: 30 + 80 + 16.
Then I add: 30 + 80 + 16 = 126. The tickets cost $126.

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: Suppose the student tickets cost 2³ dollars each instead of $2. The expression becomes 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2³.
Powers come before multiplying, so evaluate 2³ first: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
Then add: 30 + 80 + 64 = 174. The order now costs $174.

youDo.title: Your turn
lines: Seven friends split a bill. The pizzas cost 3² dollars each and they order 4 of them, plus a $6 delivery fee.
Write ONE numerical expression for the total bill.
Evaluate it: which do you handle first, the power or the multiplication?
Then divide the total among the 7 friends, and say what each step meant.

cards.text: Handle the exponent before anything else here

discourse.prompt: Two students evaluate 3 + 4 × 2 and get 14 and 11. Which one followed the order of operations, and why does the order have to be agreed on at all?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The correct value is ___ because ___ comes before ___. Without an agreed order, the same expression would have ___ values.

diagram.intro: Evaluate using the order of operations, one operation per line — I'll check each line keeps the same value.

choiceFeedback: That adds first: (6 + 2) × 5.
That subtracts instead of adding.
That ignores the 6.
That is 4 × 2 — multiplying by the exponent instead of repeating the factor.
That adds 4 + 2.

hints: The exponent says how many 4s to multiply.

optional.explanation: A numerical expression is numbers and operations with no equal sign and no variable.
choiceFeedback: That has an equal sign, which makes it an equation.
That contains a variable, so it is an algebraic expression.
A lone number has no operation to carry out.
hints: An expression shows an operation waiting to be done.

optional.stem: Sort each expression by which operation you do FIRST.
optional.explanation: Grouping symbols outrank everything; powers outrank multiplying; multiplying outranks adding and subtracting.
hints: Multiplication only wins when neither is present.

optional.stem: Match each power to its value.
optional.explanation: Each power is repeated multiplication of the base, as many times as the exponent says.

optional.title: Find the error
optional.correctWork: Step 1 adds before the power is evaluated, and it also attaches the exponent to the sum. The exponent belongs only to the 3: 3² = 9, so 2 + 9 = 11.
optional.explanation: An exponent applies to the number directly beneath it, unless parentheses say otherwise.
hints: What does the ² sit on?

choiceFeedback: That adds first: (3 + 4) × 2. Multiplication comes first.
That multiplies everything together.
That subtracts instead of adding.
hints: Which operation comes first in the order of operations?

approaching.explanation: The exponent says how many times the base is used as a factor, so 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies the base by the exponent — a common mix-up.
That uses the exponent as the base.
An exponent means repeated multiplication, not repeated addition.
hints: Which number is the base, and which is the exponent?
The exponent counts how many 2s are multiplied.
Write out the repeated multiplication the exponent asks for, then compare it with the choices.

approaching.stem: Sofia buys 4 tickets at $20 each and 2 tickets at $15 each. Which expression shows the total?
approaching.explanation: Each ticket type is a count times a price, and the two costs are added: 4 × 20 + 2 × 15.
choiceFeedback: Adding the counts to the prices loses the meaning of "each".
That multiplies total tickets by total prices, which is not what was bought.
That pairs the counts with each other and the prices with each other.
hints: What does "each" tell you to do?
Write one product per ticket type.
Then join the two costs with addition.

choiceFeedback: That computes 5 × 2 + 3. An exponent is not multiplication by the exponent.
That adds before applying the power.
That applies the power to the sum: (5 + 3)².

approaching.instructions: Evaluate each expression, following the order of operations.
approaching.hint: Powers before multiplying; grouping symbols before everything.

approaching.title: Find the error
approaching.correctWork: Step 1 adds before the rest of the expression is handled. The order of operations puts the power first (2² = 4), then the multiplication (4 × 4 = 16), and addition last: 3 + 16 = 19.
approaching.explanation: Working left to right feels natural, but addition is the LAST stage. The agreed order is what makes one expression have exactly one value.
hints: Which stage comes first: adding or the power?
Then multiply, and add only at the end.

onLevel.instructions: Sofia buys 2 member tickets ($15), 4 non-member tickets ($20), and 8 student tickets (2³ dollars). Build the total.
onLevel.hint: Evaluate the power before multiplying in the student row.

choiceFeedback: 126 uses $2 student tickets instead of 2³ = $8 each.
That treats 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6, giving 30 + 80 + 48 + extra.
That multiplies the three products together instead of adding them.

onLevel.stem: Sort each item into the stage of the order of operations where it is handled.
onLevel.explanation: Each stage finishes completely before the next begins, and within a stage you work left to right.
hints: What gets done before anything else?

onLevel.stem: Miguel evaluates 12 − 2 × 3 and gets 30. Margaret gets 6. Who is right?
choices: Margaret, because multiplication comes before subtraction
Miguel, because he worked left to right
onLevel.explanation: Multiplying first gives 2 × 3 = 6, then 12 − 6 = 6. Miguel subtracted first, getting 10 × 3 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Left to right applies only WITHIN a stage, not across stages.
One expression has exactly one value.
Margaret's 6 is correct.

onLevel.title: Find the error
onLevel.correctWork: Step 1 multiplies the base by the exponent. A power is repeated multiplication: 3² = 3 × 3 = 9, so the expression evaluates to 20 − 9 = 11.
onLevel.explanation: Step 2's arithmetic is fine — the error is entirely in what 3² means. Reading an exponent as a multiplier is the most common power mistake.
hints: 3² means 3 used as a factor twice.

extending.title: Find the error
extending.correctWork: Step 2 multiplies before applying the exponent. Once the parentheses give 8, the power comes next: 8² = 64. Then multiply, 2 × 64 = 128, and add last: 4 + 128 = 132.
extending.explanation: The exponent belongs to the parenthesis, not to the product. Squaring after multiplying squares the 2 as well, which the expression never asked for.
hints: Step 1 is correct. What does the exponent apply to?
The ² sits on the parentheses, so square 8 before multiplying.

extending.stem: Seven friends split the bill for a pizza party. They order 4 pizzas at 3² dollars each, plus a one-time $6 delivery fee. Write ONE numerical expression for what each friend owes, evaluate it, and explain why the grouping symbols matter.
extending.sampleAnswer: Each friend owes (4 × 3² + 6) ÷ 7. Evaluating: the power first, 3² = 9; then multiply, 4 × 9 = 36; then add inside the grouping symbols, 36 + 6 = 42; then divide, 42 ÷ 7 = $6 each. The grouping symbols matter because without them the expression would read 4 × 3² + 6 ÷ 7, which divides only the delivery fee among the friends and leaves each of them paying for all four pizzas — about $36.86 instead of $6. The parentheses are what say "split the WHOLE bill."
hints: Write the cost of the pizzas first, using the power.
Add the one-time fee before dividing.
What tells the reader to divide the whole total, not just the last term?

extending.instructions: Evaluate each expression. Watch the stage each one tests.
extending.hint: Compare each pair: the grouping symbols change which operation happens first.
hints: Without parentheses, division comes before addition.

optionalActivity.name: Order of Operations Sound Check

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake with powers is multiplying the base by the exponent: reading 3² as 3 × 2 = 6 instead of 3 × 3 = 9. A second is evaluating strictly left to right, so 3 + 4 × 2 becomes 14 instead of 11. The order of operations exists so one expression has exactly one value: grouping symbols, then powers, then × and ÷ left to right, then + and − left to right.

diagram.title: Rideshare Fare by Miles
diagram.caption: Each bar shows 2.50 + 1.75m evaluated for that many miles; substitute m = 8 to get the $16.50 fare, and see the base $2.50 plus $1.75 for every mile.

connect.scenario: A rideshare app charges $2.50 plus $1.75 per mile. The expression for the fare is 2.50 + 1.75m, where m is miles traveled. Your friend lives 8 miles away.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the ride cost? How does the expression model this situation?
connect.prompt: The ride costs $___ because 2.50 + 1.75(___) = ___. The 2.50 is the ___ and 1.75 is the ___.

choices: A flat base fee charged no matter how far you go
check.explanation: 2.50 has no variable attached, so it is the constant — the flat fee you pay on any ride.

choices: The cost per mile, multiplied by the number of miles
check.explanation: 1.75 is the coefficient of m, so it is the rate: $1.75 for every mile traveled.

connect.modelAnswer: Substitute m = 8: 2.50 + 1.75(8) = 2.50 + 14 = $16.50. The 2.50 is the constant base fee charged on every ride, and the 1.75 is the coefficient — the rate charged per mile.

exitTicket.explanation: Powers first: 2³ = 8. Then multiply left to right: 2 × 15 = 30 and 8 × 8 = 64. Then add: 30 + 64 = 94.
choiceFeedback: That treats 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6, giving 30 + 48 + 46. An exponent means repeated multiplication, not multiplication by the exponent.
That adds before multiplying: (2 × 15 + 8) × 8. Multiplication comes before addition.
That leaves the power unevaluated: 30 + 8 × 15 is not the expression given.
hints: What must be evaluated before any multiplying?
After the power, multiply left to right, then add.
